handoff.purpose: run_gate: advisory regression ratchet comparing current tier1 results to baseline

symbols.name: run_gate
symbols.note: Runs tier1, compares per-task recall against baseline, splits errors/focus-withheld, returns advisory gate result

claims.text: ADVISORY regression ratchet. Replays tasks (default TASKS) against a stored baseline.json and flags any PRIMARY-tier task whose recall DECREASED.
claims.why: Calls run_tier1(tasks), loads baseline, and for primary-tier tasks with base entries compares cur_recall < base_recall into regressions.

claims.text: Compares PER TASK, never on a mean -- a mean hides one task collapsing while another improves
claims.why: Loop over result['per_task'] compares each task's recall individually; no mean or aggregate used.

claims.text: Workflow before shipping a slice-heuristic change: python -m daedalus.eval --gate
claims.why: CLI wiring is in another module; this chunk only defines run_gate and does not reference __main__ or argparse.
No assertion or default expectation in this function; PASS is a CLI/report-level concept not present here.

claims.text: A FAIL means either a real regression (fix the slicer) or an intentional, reviewed label change -- in which case update the baseline EXPLICITLY (never automatically): python -m daedalus.eval --update-baseline
claims.why: The function never mutates baseline; it only reads via load_baseline. The update-baseline command and slicer fix are outside this chunk.

claims.text: GUARDRAIL: this gate is ADVISORY ONLY. It is a local developer command plus a unit test (there is no CI in this repo -- verified: no .github/workflows). It must never be wired to block an autonomous action.
claims.why: The advisory flag is set in the return (advisory: True) but the claim about CI absence and never being wired to block is external to this function; no autonomous wiring exists in this chunk.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (see run_tier1) have no recall to compare and are SPLIT by tier, not folded into regressions
claims.why: If 'error' in t, row is appended to errored_primary or errored_quarantine and continue skips regression comparison.

claims.text: PRIMARY tier -- FAILS the gate loudly (errored_primary, named in the rendered report). A broken primary-corpus task means the gate itself can no longer vouch for that task at all, which must scream exactly like a real recall regression would.
claims.why: passed is len(regressions)==0 and len(errored_primary)==0, so errored_primary fails the gate. The 'scream' and 'rendered report' aspects are outside this chunk but the fail condition is present.

claims.text: QUARANTINE tier -- reported only (errored_quarantine), never fails the gate -- flywheel debris (an unconfirmed minted task whose target moved/vanished) must not be able to block a developer's gate run.
claims.why: errored_quarantine is collected and returned but not included in the passed condition; passed only checks regressions and errored_primary.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file -- lane A1) are likewise SPLIT OUT, not folded into regressions
claims.why: If t.get('focus_withheld') is truthy, appended to focus_withheld and continue; no regression comparison.

claims.text: a task that TRANSITIONS to focus-withheld this run has no recall to compare (fail-closed is not 'recall dropped to 0'), so treating it as a regression would be a false alarm on the fence doing its job.
claims.why: The claim about transition semantics and the fail-closed floor is defined in lane A1 code elsewhere; this chunk only skips comparison when focus_withheld flag is present.

claims.text: Reported in its own focus_withheld section, regardless of tier, and never fails the gate.
claims.why: focus_withheld is returned as a separate key and not included in the passed condition; no tier filtering before the focus_withheld append.

observations.what: The function compares recall strictly with <; equal recall is neither regression nor improvement, so a task with identical recall is not listed in either regressions or improved. The docstring says 'flags any PRIMARY-tier task whose recall DECREASED', which is consistent, but the 'improved' list is returned and could be used elsewhere; no claim about equality handling is made.

new_tasks are those in current run but missing from baseline; missing_tasks are those in baseline but not in current run. The gate's passed condition ignores new_tasks and missing_tasks, so a brand-new task or a vanished task does not fail the gate. The docstring does not specify whether new or missing tasks should fail, so this is not a broken claim but an unaddressed aspect.

The passed condition is len(regressions)==0 and len(errored_primary)==0. It does not consider focus_withheld, errored_quarantine, new_tasks, or missing_tasks, matching the docstring's statements that quarantine and focus-withheld never fail the gate.

The function uses result from run_tier1(tasks) which is called with the provided tasks; the docstring says 'default TASKS' but the function default is None and uses all_tasks() -- all_tasks() is defined elsewhere and may or may not return TASKS. This is uncheckable here.
observations.where: tasks = all_tasks() if tasks is None else tasks
